prompt_en: Create one cinematic editorial photograph of Gaslamp Fantasy: visible magic operating within a gaslit nineteenth-century city. The main subject is a fictional woman guided by the supplied appearance reference. Use the supplied image only for her facial likeness and her short straight dark bob with wispy fringe. She is a municipal lamplight inspector at the end of a rainstorm, working beside an open iron utility cabinet on a narrow stone canal bridge at night. She wears a fitted oxblood wool work jacket, cream open-collar shirt and dark high-waisted trousers, her calm concentration and rain-bright face carrying a subtle personal magnetism. Her left hand steadies the cabinet door by its outer edge while her right hand grips and turns one brass stopcock at waist height; her forearms approach from separate sides without crossing, and both hands and the pipe connection are clearly visible. A pale translucent spirit flows from the exposed brass gas pipe, its upper body gathering into a small humanlike silhouette beside her shoulder while its lower trail stays visibly continuous with the pipe. The cabinet is mounted immediately below the nearest streetlamp on the same iron post. A single exposed supply pipe remains visible from the stopcock up the post to the lamp. Inside the clear glazed lamp housing, a small blue-white open flame rises directly from a visible metal burner. This newly lit lamp and the spirit cast cool light onto her face and wet fingertips; the next two streetlamps remain warm amber. Her eyes follow the newly lit lamp with a restrained, relieved half-smile. Behind her, soot-dark brick houses and a horse-drawn night carriage recede along the canal; a single covered pedestrian pauses beneath an amber lamp. Photograph the woman from mid-thigh upward at three-quarter angle, with her face, both hands, the open cabinet, the complete exposed pipe route and the connected streetlamp all readable in one frame. The camera is just below her eye level, a natural 50mm photographic perspective; moderate depth of field holds her face, hands and nearby lamp sharp, keeps the middle-distance canal houses recognizable and lets the far carriage lose fine detail with distance. Blue-white magical light, amber gaslight and deep wet burgundy form a restrained palette. Tactile wool, oxidized brass, damp stone and softly imperfect skin; grounded photographic textures, practical shadow and coherent reflections. The ordinary city has accepted this small supernatural maintenance task as part of its night work.
